_comment: Worked example (the fictional Larderloop 'whole Sunday' demo). Creative fields — creator.brief.*, creator.voice, creator.lipsync_output, voiceover.outputs.*, scenes[].vo / top_visual, captions.style / ass_sidecar, plus the brand identity (brand_name, campaign, title, layout.divider_color, endcard) — come from the calling recipe's choices (creator_gender, creator_age, creator_look, setting, tone, caption_style) and the user's brand; never copy them as defaults. Copy the STRUCTURE to config.json and fill it for this brand. A ~40s 9:16 two-zone ad where an AI creator anchor (VEED Fabric lip-sync) fills the bottom ~48% and real Larderloop app UI screen-recordings run uncropped in the top ~52%, a 3px brand-color divider between. The creator delivers the WHOLE VO cold-to-camera and each top clip PROVES its VO line's claim. Pipeline: (1) lock the script into 6 scenes + ElevenLabs eleven_v3 with-timestamps VO + per-scene timing.json; (2) gpt-image creator anchor + ONE VEED Fabric 1.0 @720p lip-sync take of the whole VO (paid, the largest spend); (3) source 16:9 top clips + the scene-1 hook graphic; (4) assemble.py two-zone composite (contain-fit + blurred-cover fill + 3px divider + creator slice), hard-concat + end card; (5) transcribe the ASSEMBLED cut + burn serif-accent word captions. Master 1080x1920 h264+aac 30fps, ~40.37s. See scripts/PIPELINE.md.
title: Larderloop — the dinner plan that plans itself

layout._comment: Two-zone split. TOP ~52% (top_height 998) runs the 16:9 UI screen-recording contain-fit + a darkened blurred cover-scale fill of the SAME clip (never black/charcoal bars). Brand-color divider (keep stacked heights EVEN: 998+4+918=1920, or libx264 rejects the odd frame). BOTTOM ~48% is the creator lip-sync framed head-to-shoulders: scale-to-width x a small ZOOM (~1.15-1.2) then crop with a DOWNWARD offset so the face is upper-middle and the shoulders enter (a plain crop-toward-top shows only the head and cuts the shoulders). Requires a MEDIUM chest-up anchor (see creator._comment).

creator._comment: ONE AI-creator anchor lip-synced to the WHOLE VO in ONE VEED Fabric 1.0 take @ 720p (480p reads soft). THE ANCHOR MUST BE a PHOTOREAL, candid MEDIUM chest-up shot at natural webcam distance (whole head with headroom + shoulders + upper chest, real lived-in room, anti-AI skin cues) — NOT a plain-background close-up headshot (reads as AI) and NOT a phone-selfie / arm-extended pose copied from another format (wrong for a fixed talking-head, and too-close can't be reframed). Watch the source video and match its creator distance. gpt-image-2, quality high, 1024x1536. VEED handles photoreal fine. VEED Fabric is a NO-ATOM paid step: image_url = the anchor, audio_url = voiceover/vo-arlo.mp3; billed per second of VO, the largest spend. Run its calls SEQUENTIALLY with sleep 3 — veed/fabric-1.0 storage-auth 403s under parallel load. Trying a 2nd voice after the lip-sync DOUBLES that spend — lock the voice first. Re-run VEED only when the anchor IMAGE changes; a crop/zoom tweak is a free re-assemble.

brief._comment: Asked of the user upstream (choices creator_gender / creator_age / creator_look / setting). These are the demo's answers — never reuse the demo creator.
brief.look: East Asian woman with a short bob and round glasses (demo only)
brief.vibe_setting: lived-in kitchen, open shelves with jars, window daylight

creator.anchor_shot: medium chest-up, natural webcam distance, headroom + shoulders — not a tight close-up, not a phone selfie

voiceover._comment: The creator delivers the ENTIRE VO cold-to-camera — the VO IS the audio bed (no music). ElevenLabs eleven_v3 with-timestamps -> voiceover/vo-arlo.mp3 + timestamp JSON. Per-scene start/end sliced from the char timestamps into voiceover/timing.json. speed 1.2 (creator-native VO reads ~1.15-1.2x).

scenes.vo: Okay, planning a week of dinners used to eat my whole Sunday and three grocery runs. Watch this.
scenes.top_visual: Scene-1 hook graphic — a kinetic 'a whole Sunday + 3 grocery runs' title-card (HTML-rendered, NOT a demo clip).
scenes.notes: Scene 1 is the designed hook graphic, not a product clip.

scenes.vo: I gave Larderloop one photo of my fridge — basically, use what's here, feed two adults, keep it under thirty minutes. And it just went.
scenes.top_visual: Larderloop taking the one fridge photo and kicking off — the UI accepts the request and starts working.
scenes.notes: The clip shows the exact photo going in and the app starting.

scenes.vo: It spotted every single ingredient, flagged what was about to go off, and checked it against, like, four hundred recipes at once.
scenes.top_visual: Ingredients tagged in the photo, near-expiry items flagged, recipe matches scrolling in.
scenes.notes: Set top_start/top_end to the on-message window — never loop a short clip.

scenes.vo: And in a few seconds, it literally laid out seven dinners AND built a grocery list sorted by aisle that I can actually tick off.
scenes.top_visual: The seven-dinner plan filling in + the aisle-sorted grocery list being ticked off.
scenes.notes: The clip proves the plan + list claim as it is said.

scenes.vo: Oh — and it set itself to re-plan every Sunday based on whatever is left over.
scenes.top_visual: The weekly auto re-plan setting being switched on in the UI.

scenes.vo: Like, look at that. It didn't send me to a recipe blog. It didn't give me homework. It just planned the whole week. That's Larderloop.
scenes.top_visual: The finished week plan into the Larderloop end card (held on the last SHARP frame ~3s).
scenes.notes: Note the last SHARP second before any fade-to-black as endcard.clip_end.

endcard._comment: The Larderloop end card held on the last SHARP frame ~3s. If the end-card clip fades to black, hold the last sharp second (clip_end), NOT the black tail.

captions._comment: Word-level captions burned from the ASSEMBLED cut (transcribe master-precaption.mp4 with local faster-whisper, NOT vo-arlo.mp3 — concat drops inter-scene silence so the ad timeline != the VO timeline). Sentence-aware chunking. style comes from choices.caption_style (serif-accent / kinetic-pop / neon-glow / clean-bubble); the demo uses serif-accent. Kept: master-precaption cut + captions/serif-accent.ass sidecar for restyle without re-render.

audio_mix._comment: The creator VO is the entire audio bed — no separate music to duck under. Body audio = the concatenated creator VO slices; the end card holds under the VO tail.

vo.note: the creator's ElevenLabs VO IS the audio bed; the lip-sync drives the mouth (no music)

captions.note: word-level captions burned from the ASSEMBLED cut (in captions.style), tracking the ad timeline not the raw VO

divider.note: a 3px brand-color divider between the two zones

endcard.note: the brand's end card (Larderloop in the demo) held on the last sharp frame ~3s
